extracted.intended_audience: organizations and individual applicants who will register and apply for federal grants using Grants.gov
extracted.subtask_short: apply for federal grants via Grants.gov
extracted.subtask_description: Step‑by‑step operational guidance for registering, creating profiles and workspaces, completing forms, naming and uploading files, and submitting federal grant applications through Grants.gov. Covers individual and organizational applicants, roles/privileges, online vs offline workflows, and troubleshooting/contacting support.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM.gov registration and UEI requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Your organization must register with SAM.gov. SAM.gov will provide a unique entity identifier (UEI) for your organization, which is required to apply for grants using Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have what’s needed by SAM.gov, including validated address and Tax ID, allow up to 10 business days for SAM registration — start as soon as possible. Your SAM.gov registration must be active at time of submission (see submission prerequisites).

rubrics_metrics.name: Login.gov account required for each Grants.gov user
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Grants.gov user who wants to download forms or work on them online must have an account with Login.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you register at Grants.gov you will be prompted to link your Grants.gov account to your Login.gov account. Everyone must create a Grants.gov profile (organization or individual) to use the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use same email across Grants.gov and SAM.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the same email address here and at SAM.gov (for your organization's electronic business point of contact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your Grants.gov account has the same email as the SAM.gov electronic business point of contact, Grants.gov will automatically assign you an expanded AOR role (superuser). This simplifies role assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a Grants.gov profile (every user)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every person who uses Grants.gov to apply for a grant must create a profile, whether they download forms to fill them out or use a workspace to fill out forms online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On the Grants.gov home page click Register, complete the registration form, confirm via temporary code emailed to you, then create an Organization Applicant Profile to apply on behalf of an organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization Applicant Profile must include UEI and identifying info
rubrics_metrics.description: You must create an Organization Applicant Profile and enter the UEI obtained from SAM.gov, a profile name, and a job title for the person who will be using the profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profile name can be organization name or any label you use to refer to the profile; job title helps other users. After entering info click Save and Login.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roles and privileges — at least one user with application-creation and submit roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov allows assignment of roles/privileges; at least one person in your organization must have a role that allows them to create a workspace (expanded AOR, standard AOR, or workspace manager). Expanded AOR or standard AOR can submit applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your Grants.gov account shares the SAM.gov electronic business POC email, you’ll be auto-assigned expanded AOR. For more info, see Manage Roles for Applicant in Grants.gov Online Help. Role assignment controls who can create workspaces, control access, view budgets, and sign & submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose workspace approach appropriate to organization complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three workspace approaches — Basic, Intermediate, and Advanced — which control how forms and access are managed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic: fill forms online or download PDFs to work offline; good for simple teams. Intermediate: workspace owner controls access to forms; useful when preparer is not the submitter. Advanced: owner can grant access to people without the UEI, limit access to budget forms, create subforms, and reuse forms; includes videos and help links. Use provided step‑by‑step guides to pick and implement the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: One workspace per grant application
rubrics_metrics.description: You must create a different workspace for each grant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To create: select grant opportunity (Search Grants or enter NOFO number), click Apply, name your grant application, select profile (or a workspace owner if you lack ownership privileges), then click Create Workspace. The Manage Workspace page appears and you can add participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding participants to a workspace
rubrics_metrics.description: You can add people to your application's workspace to help with your grant application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Manage Workspace -> Participants tab use Add from Workspace Organization to include users who have an Organization Applicant Profile, or Add by Username to include registered users without an organization profile (search by name or email). Click Save after adding participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completing forms — three methods (online, download/upload, reuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms may be completed online within the workspace, downloaded and completed offline, or reused from previously completed forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the method that fits your workflow: online Webforms for live collaborative editing; download/edit/upload for offline work (requires Adobe Reader); or reuse previously completed forms (see reuse rules below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Webform completion behaviors and checks
rubrics_metrics.description: When completing forms online, open the form via the Forms tab Webform link and navigate with the Sections menu; required fields are marked with asterisks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system auto-saves every five minutes; click Save periodically to post changes. Use the Check for Errors button to display any issues; resolve errors before re-checking. You may be prompted to lock the form; locked forms cannot be accessed by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offline form completion and upload protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: To complete forms offline you must have Adobe Reader. Download the form, optionally lock it to prevent online edits while working, complete it locally, run Check for Errors, and then upload it to your workspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Check for Errors finds issues, a pop-up lists them and highlights errors in red on the form — resolve and save before re-checking. After upload you will be asked whether to unlock the form; selecting Yes allows others to make changes to the uploaded version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locking behavior for downloaded forms
rubrics_metrics.description: When downloading a form you will be asked if you want to lock the form; selecting Yes prevents changes to the online version while you are working offline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When uploading back to the workspace you can choose to unlock the form (allow others to edit) or leave it locked. Consider locking to avoid edit conflicts when multiple people might work on the same form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required fields are marked with asterisks
rubrics_metrics.description: Asterisks mark required information on forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all asterisked fields are completed; Check for Errors will surface omissions or invalid entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Check for Errors / Check Application before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submission use the form-level Check for Errors and the workspace-level Check Application button to find and resolve issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve all listed errors before attempting to Sign and Submit. The Check Application button will list issues across the application; fix them and re-run the check until there are no blocking errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming rules for uploads
rubrics_metrics.description: Before naming files for upload, review the NOFO for agency-specific file naming instructions. If none are provided, be descriptive but follow Grants.gov limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit each file name to 50 characters or fewer. Give a unique name to each document. Allowed characters: upper- and lowercase letters, numbers, underscore (_), hyphen (-), space, and period (.). See Special Characters in Submissions for known limitations of grantor systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reusing previously completed forms overwrites prior uploads
rubrics_metrics.description: You can reuse any form that was previously completed in, or uploaded to, a Grants.gov workspace, but reusing a form will overwrite any previously uploaded version and any related subforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reusing, a popup warns about overwrite. Use the Reuse link, search, Preview the form to confirm it contains the information you want, then Select to import it into the new application. Confirm only if you intend to replace prior content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission prerequisites for Sign and Submit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sign and Submit button is available only to users with a standard or expanded AOR role (or a custom role with submit privileges) and only when several conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for availability: the forms selected for submission have passed the Check Application process; your organization's SAM.gov registration is active (Manage Workspace header shows expiration date); the grant application deadline has not passed. If these are true you (with appropriate role) can Sign and Submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and Notify AOR for non-AOR users
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not have an AOR role, use the Complete and Notify AOR button (if available) to notify organization users with an AOR role that the application is ready to submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clicking the button sends an email to AORs or users with Submit Applications privileges informing them the application is ready for final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission behavior and tracking preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are resubmitting an application, the system will ask if you want this submission to replace the previous one. If you submitted from the same workspace, the previous grant tracking number will be preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Yes to replace the prior submission. Be aware of whether you are submitting from the same workspace to retain tracking continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking application status and agency notification
rubrics_metrics.description: You can check whether your application has been received by the awarding agency via Check Application Status. The awarding agency will notify you after they complete their own process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the tracking information and agency notifications to confirm receipt and follow-up on any agency actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness — submit well before the deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: It is best to submit your application well before the deadline to allow time to resolve submission errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start SAM.gov and Grants.gov registration early (SAM may take up to 10 business days). Use Check Application and address issues in advance. Late submissions or unresolved errors can prevent acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and training resources are available
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov provides 24/7 support via phone and email and offers training resources and videos for help with registration and applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call 1-800-518-4726 or email support@grants.gov to open a ticket (you'll receive a ticket number). For SAM.gov help call 866-606-8220 or chat with the Federal Service Desk. Use Training Resources and Videos for Grants.gov to learn workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: System auto-save and session expiration behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The Grants.gov system automatically saves form work every five minutes and sessions may expire (unsaved changes will be lost if session ends).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the system auto-saves, click Save periodically to ensure changes are posted. Watch for session-expiration prompts (example: 'Your session will expire in 3 minutes') and confirm to continue working to avoid losing unsaved edits.
